- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above recent high.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.00) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for downward bias.
- Model frequently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or weak; adjust downward bias by 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment peaks near end of history, model often fails to anticipate sharp drop; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effect.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
